pillar: Bone and Soft Tissue Sarcoma Treatment in India for International Patients

items.q: Is limb-sparing surgery an option for bone sarcoma
items.a: Limb-sparing surgery, which removes the tumor while reconstructing the bone and joint instead of amputating the limb, may be considered for many bone sarcoma patients, depending on tumor size, location, and whether nearby nerves or blood vessels are involved. For osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma, chemotherapy is typically given before and after surgery to shrink the tumor and improve the chances that limb-sparing reconstruction is feasible. In cases where the tumor has spread extensively or critical structures cannot be preserved, amputation may still be recommended instead. Final decisions on surgical approach should be made by the treating oncology and orthopedic oncology team after reviewing imaging and biopsy results.

items.q: What is the difference between bone sarcoma and soft tissue sarcoma
items.a: Bone sarcomas such as osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, chondrosarcoma, and chordoma arise directly in bone tissue, while soft tissue sarcomas such as liposarcoma, synovial sarcoma, GIST, and rhabdomyosarcoma develop in muscle, fat, nerves, or connective tissue. Osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma occur more often in children and young adults, whereas chondrosarcoma and chordoma are more common in adults. Soft tissue sarcoma subtypes vary widely in behavior and treatment approach, ranging from wide local excision to targeted drug therapy for GIST. Because both groups include many distinct subtypes, treatment planning depends on confirmed histology and biomarker profile, and should be guided by a multidisciplinary sarcoma team.

Ewing sarcoma is generally treated with multi-drug chemotherapy combined with surgery, radiation, or both, with the specific combination depending on whether the tumor can be fully resected. Chemotherapy is usually given both before and after local treatment to address microscopic disease that may have spread beyond the primary tumor site. Because Ewing sarcoma can occur in bone or soft tissue and often affects children and young adults, care is typically coordinated through a pediatric or sarcoma-focused multidisciplinary team. The exact sequence and duration of treatment depends on cancer type, stage, biomarker profile, prior treatment, and specialist review, and should be discussed with a qualified oncology team.

items.q: Can GIST be treated with targeted therapy instead of surgery
items.a: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) are typically treated with a combination of surgery and targeted therapy, such as imatinib, rather than targeted therapy alone, particularly for tumors with KIT or PDGFRA mutations. Targeted drugs work by blocking the specific mutated proteins driving tumor growth and may be used before surgery to shrink a tumor or afterward to reduce recurrence risk. Whether targeted therapy can reduce the extent of surgery needed, or whether surgery alone is sufficient, depends on tumor size, mutation status, and location. This determination requires molecular testing and should be discussed with a qualified oncology team before treatment begins.

items.q: Why is surgery the main treatment for chondrosarcoma
items.a: Chondrosarcoma is primarily treated with surgery because this bone sarcoma subtype generally responds less well to standard chemotherapy and radiation compared with other sarcomas. Complete surgical removal of the tumor, sometimes with wide margins, is usually the most effective way to control the disease long-term. Because chemotherapy and radiation have limited effectiveness for most chondrosarcoma cases, treatment planning focuses heavily on achieving a complete resection while preserving function where possible. Whether limb-sparing techniques or more extensive surgery is needed depends on tumor grade, size, and location, and should be confirmed by a specialist surgical oncology team.

items.q: What tests are needed to diagnose and stage a sarcoma before treatment
items.a: Diagnosing and staging a suspected sarcoma typically requires an MRI of the affected area, a core needle biopsy with immunohistochemistry (IHC) to confirm tumor type, and often molecular or next-generation sequencing (NGS) testing to identify relevant mutations. MRI helps define tumor size and involvement of surrounding structures, while biopsy and IHC confirm the specific sarcoma subtype, which guides treatment choice. Molecular testing is particularly relevant for tumors such as GIST, where mutation status can determine targeted therapy eligibility. Which combination of tests is needed depends on the suspected sarcoma type and should be guided by a specialist sarcoma team before any biopsy or surgery is scheduled locally.

items.q: How much does sarcoma treatment cost in India
items.a: Sarcoma treatment costs in India vary by subtype and procedure, with approximate planning ranges of $6,000 to $15,000 for limb-sparing bone sarcoma surgery, $3,500 to $10,000 for soft tissue sarcoma surgery, $600 to $2,000 per chemotherapy cycle, and $3,000 to $7,000 for a radiation therapy course. These figures are estimated ranges only and vary further depending on reconstruction complexity, number of chemotherapy cycles, and radiation technique used. A confirmed cost estimate can only be provided after a treating hospital reviews the patient's MRI, biopsy, and molecular testing results, since final costs depend on cancer type, stage, biomarker profile, prior treatment, and specialist review.

items.q: Which hospitals in India treat sarcoma
items.a: Experienced sarcoma treatment centers in India are concentrated in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru, with additional regional capability in Ahmedabad and Kochi. Delhi NCR and Mumbai offer strong orthopedic and radiation oncology programs alongside international patient services, while Chennai and Bengaluru have experienced surgical oncology teams and multidisciplinary tumor boards, and Hyderabad has growing access to proton therapy. Because sarcoma care depends heavily on a multidisciplinary team rather than a single doctor, hospital and city selection should be based on the specific sarcoma subtype and treatment plan, and confirmed through specialist review before travel is arranged.

items.q: What does the process of getting sarcoma treatment in India involve
items.a: Getting sarcoma treatment in India generally follows a defined sequence: sharing MRI, biopsy, and IHC reports for case review, receiving a shortlist of suitable specialists and hospitals with an estimated treatment plan and cost, arranging medical visa and appointment support, traveling for final evaluation and treatment, and receiving discharge and follow-up coordination with doctors back home. Reports are typically reviewed before any local biopsy or surgery is scheduled, so specialists can weigh in on the diagnostic workup itself. The exact timeline and sequence can vary depending on sarcoma subtype, treatment complexity, and specialist availability, and should be confirmed with the treating team.

items.q: How can CancerFax help patients seeking sarcoma treatment in India
items.a: CancerFax helps patients organize medical reports, identify relevant specialists or trials, estimate costs, and coordinate travel, visa, and follow-up support alongside the treating oncology team. For sarcoma patients specifically, this includes sharing MRI, biopsy, and IHC reports with the medical coordination team before local procedures are scheduled, and receiving a shortlist of experienced sarcoma specialists matched to the confirmed subtype and stage. CancerFax does not make treatment decisions or replace the oncologist; all diagnosis, staging, and treatment choices remain with the treating medical team, and any recommendations should be confirmed through specialist review.
